cluster_name: DR Congo Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in national history
event_summary: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC exceeded 5,000 confirmed cases and 2,300 deaths by August 19, 2026, the deadliest in the country's history. The Bundibugyo strain has spread to six provinces since May 15; no approved vaccines or treatments exist for it.
tldr: RT Africa is the only outlet to question Western policy response — framing US travel restrictions as potential overreaction while the CDC itself assessed American risk as low — while simultaneously reporting that unpaid Congolese health workers are deserting Ebola facilities, pointing to governance failure rather than pure epidemiology. The Congolese government's counter-claim that its response is 'robuste' appears exclusively in French-language African coverage (RFI Afrique), invisible to Asian, English-language, and German-language outlets that treat WHO's alarm as unchallenged. German public broadcasters (Tagesschau, Deutsche Welle) uniquely emphasize the European donor response — new Germany and EU aid — rather than the epidemiological escalation alone. Across 18 outlets in 12 countries, the dominant consensus is stark: this is the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history, spreading faster than any previous epidemic, with no approved vaccines for the Bundibugyo strain.

outlet_exclusive_vocab_highlights.what_it_reveals: Dual-outlet signature: RT Africa's governance focus (unpaid workers, travel restrictions) combined with France 24 Spanish's scientific emphasis (Bundibugyo spread rate in Spanish) — both exclusive to this bucket.
BBC Africa's fact-check angle (misinformation driving violence) and RFI's political frame (Kinshasa's riposte defense) are both exclusive to African-focused coverage.
German-language framing marks Germany as a donor state covering the outbreak through a national aid-contribution lens alongside epidemiological facts.
French outlets uniquely foreground the WHO's international spread risk warning — terms absent from English-language wire coverage of the same WHO statements.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: No US outlet appears in this cluster despite the CDC issuing travel guidance and RT Africa citing US travel restrictions; US coverage appears to have treated the story as a consular travel advisory rather than a global health emergency.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to editorialize against US travel restrictions, asking 'Is the US panicking with new travel bans?' while noting the CDC's own low-risk assessment for Americans.
Only outlet to report unpaid Congolese health workers walking off the job at Ebola facilities, introducing a labor-governance dimension to the response failure.
Only outlet to surface Kinshasa's counter-narrative that its response is 'robuste,' while also noting authorities are preparing school reopening in six affected provinces.
Only outlet to specifically report Germany and the EU increasing financial aid contributions to the DRC Ebola response.
Only outlet to quantify that the Bundibugyo variant has spread five times faster than previous Ebola strains, providing comparative epidemiological context absent from English-language wires.
BBC Verify documents specific misinformation-linked incidents of violence against health workers — the only fact-checking frame in the cluster.
Only outlet to quote an MSF physician observing that many Ebola cases are identified only after patients die in the community, meaning the case fatality ratio is not falling as the outbreak matures.

bottom_line: Across 18 outlets in 12 countries, near-total consensus holds that the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak is an unprecedented emergency — 5,000+ confirmed cases, no approved vaccines, and WHO warning it is 'far from under control.' The divergence lies not in severity but in attribution: infrastructure gaps and vaccine absence dominate Western wires; community violence and misinformation drive African and pan-Arab coverage; and RT Africa uniquely turns the lens on both DRC governance failures (unpaid workers) and Western overreaction (US travel bans).
